SMTO-SKL-0018 — SMTO couldn't tell which calendar event you meant

GUID: f7ff8b81-7580-5c3e-92d2-d9e386a2ffea
Slug: google-calendar-event-ambiguous
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • This message says several events could match your request, so SMTO couldn't tell which one to change. It comes from an older record, so check your calendar before assuming nothing changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Google Calendar and check whether the change you asked for already happened to any of the matching events. This message comes from an older record and doesn't tell us whether anything was changed.
  2. Ask SMTO to show the events that match, with their dates, times and calendars. Seeing them side by side lets you pick the one you meant.
  3. Tell SMTO exactly which event to change, by its date, time and calendar, and what to change. SMTO only changes an event it can identify exactly, never one picked by its title alone.

What success looks like

  • SMTO changes the event you chose and no other event is affected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to change every event with that title; that could change meetings you didn't mean.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A legacy google_calendar.event_ambiguous diagnostic was reported; current Calendar tools have no producer for it and require an exact calendar_id and event_id for every change, so it does not establish whether an older write ran.

What this means

  • The event-ambiguous alias is retained, but current Calendar mutations require exact event IDs and do not implement title-based mutation selection. This retained alias has no direct current emitting producer. Related source establishes the current boundary only; do not infer that a historical guard ran or prevented provider effects.

Why this can happen

  • The event-ambiguous alias is retained, but current Calendar mutations require exact event IDs and do not implement title-based mutation selection.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the emitting version and inspect bounded current candidates through read operations.

How to fix it

  • Read the candidate events with a bounded google_calendar.events search, have the user choose one, and pass that exact calendar_id and event_id (with its ETag) to the change. Do not mutate an event selected by title or query, and check the calendar's current state before repeating any older write.
  • Read event candidates and resolve the intended exact identity before changing any event.

Retry and execution caution

  • Read the bounded event candidates and ask the user which exact event to change. Do not mutate by title or query.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended exact calendar and event IDs are selected before a mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This retained alias has no direct current emitting producer. Related source establishes the current boundary only; do not infer that a historical guard ran or prevented provider effects.
